newsitem.title: USA: Campbell says threat limited to Australia unit.
newsitem.headline: Campbell says threat limited to Australia unit.

text.p: Campbell Soup Co. said Friday an extortion threat aimed at its majority-owned Australian affiliate Arnotts Ltd. was limited to parts of that country and did not pertain to other Campbell operations.

"This is a situation that is 100 percent limited to Australia and it is an Australian food industry issue," Campbell spokesman Kevin Lowery said. "They just happened to target a company that is an icon there."
The financial impact on Arnotts, Australia's largest cookie and cracker maker, was unknown, Lowery said. But he added that Arnotts represented a relatively small portion of Campbell's overall sales.
Campbell owns about 70 percent in Arnotts, whose shares fell 3 percent to A$8.50 ($6.51) in Sydney after the lifting of a trading halt Friday that was imposed as news of the extortion threat emerged.

Australian grocery chains began removing Arnotts products from their stores Friday, at the request of Arnotts, after police confirmed an extortionist had threatened to poison the company's cookies and plant them in supermarkets.

An extortion letter and packages containing cookies laced with a pesticide were received by Arnotts, politicians and a media organisation in the states of New South Wales and Queensland on Feb. 3, police said Friday.
Police said the cookies in the packages were laced after the extortionist bought them.

The letter demanded that police involved in a murder investigation of a bookmaker in 1991 undergo a lie detector test or poisoned cookies would be planted in supermarkets along Australia's east coast.

Police said the extortionist claimed that a man serving a life sentence for the execution-style murder of a bookmaker in 1991 was innocent. The extortion letter said the man was a friend and that the real killers remain free.

The extortion letter, part of which was published in an Australian newspaper Friday, said if the demands were not met, stores would be targeted throughout the Australian states of New South Wales and Queensland and a campaign of attacks would continue until the issue was resolved.
Lowery said Campbell's senior management was aware of the situation and offering its support, but that Arnotts managers were handling the crisis.
Arnotts also released half-year results on Friday, showing a 14.5 percent decline on profits from a year earlier.
In September, Arnotts reported sales of A$675 million ($517.1 million) for the year ended June 30, 1996.
Campbell had sales of $7.68 billion ($5.9 billion) for the year ended July 28, 1996.
Campbell's stock rose 50 cents to $86.875 on the New York Stock Exchange in early afternoon trading.
